rationale:
RFC_029's resolver only guesses commit_sha because no handler exposes it at a consistent name — bugs_open/334, the real gate on step 5's flip (this pair alone is 629 rows / 317 in the last 24h, growing, and the largest live conflict class). I asked the bugfix_315 lane which path is correct rather than picking one from the shape (their field, their register DGH-013/RFC_038). Their answer (committed 34cff7080, appended to the CONTRIB file): the unsuffixed handler_result alias is right by the loop's own sequential-per-item contract, but a single explicit mapping cannot work because the path inside handler_result varies by which handler ran — 9+ distinct output_field names for the underlying git_commit step. Their recommendation, which I am building: standardise at the SOURCE, one handler at a time, so complete_work_item can eventually use one explicit mapping instead of the search. I take the handler configs; the bdl-side wire is theirs, after, in that order (wiring first would silently drop the sha for every handler not yet converted).

This submission is the FIRST and highest-priority handler: page-rerender. I independently re-scoped the population before building anything, because the 315 lane's own count ("~16 agent configs") turned out to conflate two different questions. `handler_agent` is dispatched dynamically per work item; I queried the real live population from site_work_items.handler_agent (a top-level column, not inside spec) rather than trusting a static list. Of ~34 distinct handler types ever dispatched, page-rerender is 4,810 of the last 7 days' items — by far the largest, an order of magnitude over the next real one. Several agents that DO have a git_commit step (content-feed-orchestrator, nav-link-fixer, rerender-site, site-asset-renderer, model-directory-publisher, deployer-agent, site-deployer, pageflow-builder, page-rebuild, site-work-orchestrator, report-builder) have ZERO occurrences as a live handler_agent value — they are never bdl's handler, so their internal shape is irrelevant to this specific conflict class regardless of the 315 lane's step-level census. Conversely page-build-handler (662/7d, second largest) has no git_commit of its own — it reaches one indirectly by calling page-rerender — so this migration is also the precondition for that one, not just the largest fix on its own merits.

The mechanism required a real design decision, not just a value add. page-rerender's complete step declares its result via output_fields (list mode): for each string in the list, ExtractNestedField(collectedData, that_same_string) is stored under that same string as the response key — so a plain new list entry like "deploy_result.response.data.commit_sha" would produce a response key that IS that literal dotted string, invisible to any dot-path reader including the very resolver this fix serves. I tried routing through extract_fields first and rejected it too: it always wraps its result in a map, so the value arrives one nesting level too deep regardless of naming. The only mode that builds an independently-named target<-source map is result_mapping, mutually exclusive with output_fields in the platform's own precedence table (result_contract.go) — so the fix is a controlled CONVERSION, not an addition: every currently-exposed field re-declared as an identity mapping, plus one new commit_sha entry.
submitter: staged_component_build lane — RFC_029 §10.13 step 5's real gate (bdl/commit_sha), handler standardisation half, page-rerender first

plan.summary: Convert page-rerender's complete step from output_fields (list mode) to result_mapping, preserving rendered_page and deploy_result byte-for-byte via identity maps and adding one new canonical commit_sha key sourced from deploy_result.response.data.commit_sha. First of ~7 handler configs standardising the field bugs_open/334 needs; page-rerender is chosen first because it is by far the largest live bdl handler (4,810/7d) and the precondition for page-build-handler's own fix.

edits.rationale: Converts page-rerender's complete step from output_fields=["rendered_page","deploy_result"] to result_mapping={"rendered_page":"rendered_page","deploy_result":"deploy_result","commit_sha":"deploy_result.response.data.commit_sha"}. The first two entries are identity mappings of already-top-level keys, so the response is byte-identical for any existing reader of rendered_page or deploy_result; commit_sha is the one new key. Guarded: exactly 1 live row; complete still runs complete_workflow; output_fields is EXACTLY the two-entry list this file was written against (a changed list means some other field is exposed today that this file does not know to preserve, so it refuses rather than silently dropping it); deploy_page is still git_commit with output_field=deploy_result (the path this migration maps depends on both). VERIFY is a DO/RAISE block (ON_ERROR_STOP cannot stop a COMMIT on a non-empty SELECT result) asserting the exact three-key mapping, confirmed against a REAL completed orchestration's collected_data (not just that the config string is correct, but that the mapped path actually resolves against live data), plus a recursive (sub_workflow-safe) negative control that no other live step acquired this exact mapping.
edits.sketch: UPDATE agent_definitions SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config #- '{workflow,steps,complete,config,output_fields}', '{workflow,steps,complete,config,result_mapping}', jsonb_build_object('rendered_page','rendered_page','deploy_result','deploy_result','commit_sha','deploy_result.response.data.commit_sha'), true) WHERE type='page-rerender' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL; -- full guard/VERIFY/negative-control/snapshot_agent() in the file, not abbreviated here (lesson from migration 514's REVISE round: the sketch is what a reviewer sees)

edits.rationale: Restores output_fields=["rendered_page","deploy_result"] and removes result_mapping, refusing unless result_mapping is EXACTLY what 519 wrote (another session may have extended it on purpose, e.g. adding a further field for page-build-handler's own fix). Names the observable that would justify running it: an existing reader of handler_result.response treating the response as a specific structural type rather than just reading named keys — not merely 'commit_sha appeared', since that is additive and expected.
edits.sketch: default_config #- '{workflow,steps,complete,config,result_mapping}' then jsonb_set output_fields back to the two-entry list; guard checks the exact prior mapping first.

grounded_in: CONTRIB + reply exchange, docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_315_deployed_at_without_publication/CONTRIB_2026-08-20_from_staged_component_build_commit_sha_resolves_by_guess.md (their reply committed 34cff7080): confirms the unsuffixed handler_result alias is correct by build-dispatch-loop's own sequential-per-item sub_workflow contract (mark_complete already carries "result!": "handler_result"); refutes a single explicit path (9+ distinct git_commit output_field names fleet-wide, sampled evidence of 2 different real paths in 8 completed items); recommends standardising at the source; states ownership split (handler configs mine, the bdl-side wire theirs, after).

bugs_open/334 (complete_work_item's Optional commit_sha conflicts every loop iteration) — the field this migration serves; its own council-approved 090 run returned UNVERIFIABLE (iteration-cap, no information), so the mechanism rests on first-hand verification, cited here.

site_work_items.handler_agent census, run 2026-08-21 (top-level column, not inside spec — checked \d site_work_items first): page-rerender 4,810/7d (by far the largest of ~34 distinct handler types), page-build-handler 662/7d (second, and it has no git_commit of its own).

Full recursive step-graph census of every live agent with a git_commit step, cross-referenced against the handler_agent population: content-feed-orchestrator/nav-link-fixer/rerender-site/site-asset-renderer/model-directory-publisher/deployer-agent/site-deployer/pageflow-builder/page-rebuild/site-work-orchestrator/report-builder all have git_commit but ZERO occurrences as a live handler_agent value.

page-rerender's live workflow, read from agent_definitions 2026-08-21: deploy_page (git_commit, output_field=deploy_result, no error_step) -> update_status (update_page_status) -> complete (output_fields=["rendered_page","deploy_result"]); complete_skipped (reached when deploy never runs) exposes only ["rendered_page"] and is untouched by this file.

result_contract.go ResolveResultSpec/ApplyResultSpec, read at the file: output_fields (ResultModeFields) does result[fn]=ExtractNestedField(collectedData,fn) — same string as path and key; result_mapping (ResultModeMapping) does result[target]=ExtractNestedField(collectedData,src) for explicit pairs; the two are mutually exclusive in the precedence table (only the highest-precedence present key is used).

extract_fields action (v3_site_actions.go:5439) checked and rejected as an alternative: its result is always result[target]=value inside a wrapper map, so routing through it adds a nesting level rather than removing one.

Live artefact confirmation, 2026-08-21 ~12:0xZ: a real completed page-rerender orchestration's collected_data.deploy_result.response.data.commit_sha = "428c4730917449c3602e2605fbf3931047cace8b" — the exact path this migration maps, read at the data, not inferred from Go source alone.

GitCommitAction (git_deployer_actions.go) and GitHubClient.CommitToRepo (internal/adapters/git/github_client.go), read to rule out a coexisting needs_diagnosis item's claim before trusting this path: the skip branch (no files to commit) returns {success:true, metadata:{status:skipped,...}} with NO .response key at all, so ExtractNestedField(...,"deploy_result.response.data.commit_sha") on a skip correctly returns nil and ApplyResultSpec's mapping mode correctly drops the absent target — commit_sha is correctly ABSENT on a skip, matching reality, not a URL or wrong-shaped value.

Migration 512 (APPROVED, applied) and its REVISE-round lesson used directly here: put the real guard in the sketch, not a one-line summary of it — this submission's sketch quotes the guard-bearing shape rather than abbreviating it away.
plan.risks:
1. THIS IS ONE OF ~7 REAL HANDLERS, NOT THE WHOLE FIX. Six more direct handlers remain (rerender-pages, css-patch-agent, section-editor, webdesign-agent, nav-updater, each an order of magnitude smaller by volume) plus page-build-handler, whose own fix depends on THIS one shipping first (it calls page-rerender via call_agent and would map its own commit_sha from this migration's new key). Nothing is flipped by this submission; bdl still resolves commit_sha via the search until the bugfix_315 lane adds its wire, and their own stated ordering requirement is that the wire comes AFTER the config half — submitting this now, before all handlers convert, is deliberate and matches that ordering, not a jump ahead of it.

2. I AM ASSERTING NO EXISTING READER DEPENDS ON THE OUTPUT_FIELDS SHAPE SPECIFICALLY (as opposed to just the keys/values it produces). result_mapping and output_fields produce structurally identical maps for identity-mapped keys — same key names, same values — so I believe this is safe by construction, but I have not exhaustively searched every consumer of page-rerender's response for a check on the response's TYPE or PROVENANCE rather than its content. The rollback names this exact observable to watch for.

3. THE RE-SCOPING FROM ~16 TO ~7 AGENTS IS A CORRECTION TO THE 315 LANE'S OWN COUNT, made independently and stated here for their review rather than silently substituted: their count was of agents with a git_commit STEP; mine is of agents actually reachable as bdl's HANDLER. Both counts are real measurements of different populations. If I have the dispatch mechanism wrong (e.g. if some handler_agent values are resolved through an alias table I have not found, meaning a git_commit-having agent I excluded IS secretly reachable), this migration would still be correct and harmless — it only ADDS a key to page-rerender, and does not touch or exclude anything based on the wider count. The risk of a wrong re-scope is under-building, not over-building: I might do fewer migrations than are actually needed, not more.

4. A COEXISTING, UNRELATED FINDING ON THE SAME STEPS: an unclaimed needs_diagnosis work item (site_work_items id 0ed66d57, filed 2026-08-19, failed on claim-timeout before a 090 run ever executed) describes update_page_status stamping pages.deployed_at without checking deploy_result for actual success. I read the code to confirm this migration is unaffected either way (the skip path has no .response key, so commit_sha correctly resolves absent there regardless of what deployed_at claims) — and separately confirmed the underlying defect is already covered by the bugfix_315 lane's OWN shipped fix (content_hash / four live update_page_status steps, their NOTES 2026-08-20). Not this submission's concern; noted so the reviewer does not need to chase it themselves.
